prompt: I'm selling on Shopify and want to start offering product bundles to lift my average order value. Customers buy single products today; if I bundle related products with a discount I think I can get them to add more to the cart. I should be able to create and manage bundles myself from the Shopify admin — no developer help needed once it's set up. Two bundle types matter. Fixed: I pick the exact products and the customer buys the whole pack or nothing. Flexible: I define a pool and a count ("pick any 3 from this list") and the customer chooses which items they want. Each bundle should let me pick products or specific variants. The discount should be configurable per bundle. I want to choose between three discount kinds: percentage off the bundle total, a flat amount off, or buy-X-get-Y-free where one of the items is effectively included free. On top of that I want tiered discounts — the more items in the bundle the bigger the cut. For example 2 items 10% off, 3 items 20% off, 4 items 30% off. On the storefront the bundle UI should appear on the product page itself. The customer picks their items (for flexible bundles), sees the discounted total live, and adds the whole bundle to cart in one click — discount applied automatically at checkout. In the admin I want a table of all my bundles, edit any field, enable/disable per bundle, and a count of times each was bought.

intent.desiredOutcome: Merchants create and manage fixed/flexible product bundles with configurable and tiered discounts; customers pick items on the storefront, see live totals, and add to cart with one click.
intent.qualityBrief: A polished bundle app handles duplicate webhook delivery on discount creation, prevents customers from picking fewer items than required in flexible bundles, gracefully disables the widget if a bundled product is deleted or goes out of stock, and shows the merchant clear feedback when a discount tier is misconfigured (e.g., overlapping ranges). The storefront widget must calculate and display the final price instantly as items are selected, handle mobile-friendly variant selection, and include copy-to-clipboard for bundle URLs. The admin panel must validate that fixed bundles have at least 2 items and flexible bundles have a pool larger than the required count. The app must track which bundle each order came from (via order note), handle partial refunds without re-crediting the discount, and avoid applying the discount twice if the customer manually adds a discount code at checkout.

plan.dataFlow: The merchant creates a bundle (fixed or flexible) via the admin panel, which persists the bundle definition locally and creates a corresponding Shopify product bundle (productBundleCreate) plus an automatic app discount (discountAutomaticAppCreate) backed by a Shopify Function that encodes all tier and discount-kind logic via metafields. On the storefront, the widget reads the bundle definition from the app backend, renders item selection for flexible bundles, computes the discounted total live in the browser, and on "Add to Cart" calls cartCreate with all bundle lines, stamps a cart attribute with the bundle identifier, then calls cartNoteUpdate to record which bundle was bought. When an order is paid, the orders/paid webhook fires and the app records a purchase event against the bundle for count tracking. When a product in a pool is deleted or goes unavailable (products/update or products/delete), the app marks affected bundle components as unavailable and auto-disables any bundle whose required items can no longer be fulfilled, surfacing a warning in the admin. Merchants can edit any bundle field from the admin table, which calls productBundleUpdate and discountAutomaticAppUpdate in tandem, and can toggle a bundle enabled/disabled which calls discountAutomaticActivate or discountAutomaticDeactivate.

persistence.name: bundles
persistence.purpose: Master record for each merchant-created bundle, holding its type, discount configuration, Shopify resource references, and operational status.

columns.name: bundle_type
columns.purpose: fixed or flexible

columns.name: required_count
columns.purpose: for flexible bundles: how many items the customer must choose

columns.name: discount_kind
columns.purpose: percentage, flat-amount, or buy-x-get-y

columns.name: discount_value
columns.purpose: base discount amount when no tier rules override it

columns.name: availability_status
columns.purpose: active, degraded (some components unavailable), or suspended (cannot be fulfilled)

columns.name: shopify_product_external_id
columns.purpose: the Shopify product bundle node that was created for this bundle

columns.name: shopify_discount_external_id
columns.purpose: the Shopify DiscountAutomaticNode backing the bundle discount

columns.name: purchase_count
columns.purpose: running tally of orders that included this bundle

single bundle looked up by id for edit or widget rendering
bundles containing a given product external id for product-deletion fan-out

persistence.name: bundle_components

columns.name: position
columns.purpose: display ordering within the bundle

columns.name: is_available

all components across all bundles matching a given product external id (for product-change fan-out)
all components across all bundles matching a given variant external id

persistence.keyedBy: one row per (bundle, tier threshold), keyed by id
queryPatterns: all tiers for a given bundle ordered by min_quantity ascending
tiers for a set of bundles in a single fetch (for admin list view pre-load)

edgeCases: Duplicate orders/paid webhook delivery for the same order — the handler checks for an existing purchase event row keyed by (bundle id, order external id) and exits without writing if one already exists.

Customer manually enters a discount code at checkout in addition to the automatic bundle discount — the purchase event records all codes applied; the Shopify Function must be configured with combinesWith.orderDiscounts=false so the automatic bundle discount does not stack with a manual code.

A product in a flexible bundle pool is deleted before the customer adds to cart — the widget GET returns is_available=false for that component; the backend validate-and-build-cart-payload rejects any selection containing that variant and returns a user-facing error.
Flexible bundle: customer submits fewer selected items than the required count — the validate-and-build-cart-payload capability returns a validation error before any Shopify API call is made.
Fixed bundle: merchant tries to save with fewer than 2 component items — the admin create/update endpoints return a validation error listing the constraint before calling Shopify.

Tier rules have overlapping quantity ranges (e.g. tier 1: 2–4 items, tier 2: 3–5 items) — the validate-tier-configuration capability rejects the configuration with a specific overlap error message shown in the admin before any Shopify write.

productBundleCreate or discountAutomaticAppCreate returns a Shopify user error — the bundle row is saved with null Shopify reference ids and a degraded status; the merchant sees a clear error in the admin and can retry.
Partial refund on a bundle order — the purchase event is immutable; no discount credit is re-applied because the automatic discount fires only at checkout, not on refund.

hld_v_findings.issue: "integration": null and "shopifySteps": [] but description states "deactivate their Shopify discounts so customers are not shown a broken widget." The coding agent will implement this capability as a pure database write with no Shopify API call, leaving the automatic discount(s) on a paused bundle active in Shopify. The broken bundle's discount will continue firing at checkout even after the bundle is paused.
hld_v_findings.fix: Set integration to "shopify-admin" and add a shopifySteps entry that calls discountAutomaticDeactivate (consuming the shopify_discount_external_id from the affected bundles), mirroring the deactivation step already resolved in toggle-bundle-discount-active-state.

hld_v_findings.issue: "Create one automatic discount node per tier rule" means a bundle with tiers at 2, 3, and 4 items creates three simultaneous active automatic discounts scoped to the same component products. For a cart with 4 bundle items all three discounts are live concurrently and Shopify will attempt to apply each one independently — the customer gets a 10%, 20%, AND 30% discount stacked, not just the highest applicable tier. Shopify's combinesWith setting prevents stacking with other discount types but not with other automatic discounts of the same type.
hld_v_findings.fix: Replace the one-node-per-tier strategy with a single discountAutomaticBasicCreate that uses Shopify's quantity-break (stepped) pricing or, if the API does not support it natively, store tier logic app-side and apply only the highest matching tier's discount at the point of discount creation/update, deactivating the replaced tier node before creating the new one.

hld_v_findings.issue: Both columns carry role "money" but their purpose fields explicitly include percentage values (e.g. "10% off", "percentage or flat amount applying at this tier"). The spec defines money as "for currency amounts only" and ratio as "fractional values bounded between 0 and 1." A percentage stored as 10, 20, 30 fits neither money nor ratio, so the coding agent receives an ambiguous signal about the column's domain type and storage range.
hld_v_findings.fix: Split into two typed columns — one with role money (flat-amount discount) and one with role ratio (percentage discount stored as a decimal 0–1), with each nullable when the discount_kind does not use it; or keep a single value column but change its role to text and document the encoding convention, letting the coding agent choose the correct DDL.

hld_v_findings.issue: "returnsList": true is set on a write capability whose sole job is to create Shopify discount nodes. The spec defines returnsList as "the capability shows the merchant or customer multiple records they can browse, sort, filter, or paginate." This is a write (create) operation, not a read/browse operation. The flag will mislead the coding agent into generating list-pagination scaffolding for what should be a plain fire-and-persist write path.
hld_v_findings.fix: Set returnsList to false on create-tier-discounts.
